text: You just finished a tough boss fight or nailed a perfect combo. That rush is exhilarating! All you want is to dive back into the action, no delays.
But then, the inevitable happens. The screen fades, a progress bar appears, and the game enters a loading sequence. It's an unavoidable pause, pulling you out of the flow.
Your mind, accustomed to constant stimulation, starts to wander. You glance at your phone, tap your foot, or just stare blankly. Why does this wait feel so long?
Suddenly, a small, helpful tip appears on screen: 'Did you know you can sneak past patrols?' Your eyes snap back. Your brain now has a new task.
The system isn't making the loading faster. It's giving your mind something to do, preventing boredom and frustration. This mental engagement makes the wait *feel* shorter.
You're back in the game, refreshed and more informed. The loading screen wasn't just a wait; it was a carefully designed cognitive intervention.
